findings.summary: The explanation says to call iter() again for a fresh cursor, but calling iter() on an exhausted iterator returns that same iterator.
findings.evidence: The first call exhausts the iterator; call iter() again for a fresh cursor.
findings.fix: Say: 'Calling iter(it) returns the same exhausted iterator. Call iter() on the original list (or re-create the iterator) to get a fresh cursor.'
